site: de Gerlache crater rim, lunar south pole (NASA PGDA LOLA Site11)

frame.description: Local right-handed, y-up frame in meters (Three.js convention). Origin = play-area center (a Site11 pixel center). +x = polar-stereographic +X (grid east); +z = polar-stereographic -Y (grid south), so image rows increase with +z and image columns with +x. +y = up (radial).
frame.projection: South polar stereographic, lat_0=-90, lon_0=0, true scale at the pole, sphere R=1737400 m (scale error < 0.02% inside 8 km, < 0.4% at 200 km; ignored)
frame.toPolarStereo: X = originX + x ; Y = originY - z
frame.fromPolarStereo: x = X - originX ; z = originY - Y
frame.heights: All heightmaps store TANGENT-PLANE heights: LOLA elevation above the 1737.4 km sphere minus the curvature drop r^2 / (2R), r = horizontal distance from the origin. A flat-world renderer then shows the real horizon (about 2.4 km away for a 1.7 m camera on flat ground). To recover LOLA elevation: elevation = height + (x^2 + z^2) / (2 * 1737400).

towardPole.note: The south pole (and Shackleton crater) lies this way.

frame.azimuthConvention: azimuth_deg is measured from local -z, turning toward +x (clockwise seen from above). Direction vector = (x: sin(az), z: -cos(az)). For a body at infinity (Sun, Earth) the azimuth equals its sub-point longitude (deg east) to within ~0.1 deg here.

sunAndEarth.elevationFormula: sin(el) = sin(siteLat) * sin(subLat) + cos(siteLat) * cos(subLat) * cos(subLon - siteLon)
sunAndEarth.sun: Azimuth = subsolar longitude; it decreases about 12.19 deg per Earth day, so the Sun circles counterclockwise seen from above (-z -> -x -> +z -> +x). Subsolar latitude stays within +/-1.54 deg, so the Sun's elevation here is about -subLat + 1.46 * cos(az - (-67.6)) deg: highest when it is opposite the pole direction (az 292), lowest toward the pole.

earth.note: Earth sits near longitude 0, i.e. toward local -z, swinging about +/-8 deg in azimuth (libration). Its elevation is about +0.6 deg +/- 6.7 deg, so it bobs above and below the horizon over a month. Horizon height toward -z from the landing point: -0.57 deg.

coldMask.formula: psr_fraction = value / 255; value >= 128 means permanently shadowed
coldMask.source: LOLA permanent-shadow map LPSR_85S_060M (60 m), bilinear to 5 m

rockyAreas.name: Rocky area 1
rockyAreas.description: Small fresh crater; scatter boulders on its rim and out to about one crater radius. Its inner wall may be too steep to drive.

rockyAreas.name: Rocky area 2
rockyAreas.description: Small fresh crater; scatter boulders on its rim and out to about one crater radius. Its inner wall may be too steep to drive.

shadowedCrater.description: Permanently shadowed region (LOLA PSR map, Mazarico et al. 2011) in an unnamed, degraded crater on the outer (northern) flank of the de Gerlache rim

iceCandidate.name: Ice candidate
iceCandidate.note: Game ice spot: 100-200 m inside the permanent-shadow edge on the side facing the landing, fully shadowed. Not shown on the minimap; players find it by drilling.

deGerlacheFloorPSR.note: Largest LOLA permanent-shadow region within 25 km of the de Gerlache crater center (the crater floor). Visible from the rim but outside the play area.

notes: Drive distances are least-cost routes on a 20 m grid avoiding slopes over 20 deg; straight-line distances are also given.
Rocky areas are small fresh craters (compact steep patches against the regional slope); driveDistance is to the nearest drivable point within ~150 m. Place boulders densest there.

Small PSRs (< 0.1 km^2, mostly inside fresh craters) are also in cold-mask.png; one sits in Rocky area 1 if that crater is close to the landing point. Drop them from the cold zone if the freeze mechanic should only apply in the big shadowed crater.
On the de Gerlache side of the play area 43% of the ground is steeper than 20 deg at 20 m scale, but routes exist: the lowest drivable point on that side is at 165 m (landing is 1537 m).
The de Gerlache crater floor PSR is NOT inside the play area: its nearest point is 9.7 km from the landing point. The shadowed crater used here is a smaller real PSR on the rim's outer flank.
Moon sites features (coldTraps, youngCraters, boulderTrackCandidates, lowLightPatches) come from game/tools/moon_sites.py; added for review by the pipeline owner.

coldTraps: LOLA 60 m PSR fraction >= 0.5 (bilinear to 5 m), at least 2,000 m^2. Patches of one or two 60 m source pixels (sourcePixels60m) are at the map's resolution limit; horizonCheck5m repeats the test on the game's 5 m heights (whole Sun disc hidden at every azimuth for the highest Sun of the 18.6-year cycle).

youngCraters: depressions with a raised rim in the 5 m DEM. freshness 'fresh' means depth/diameter >= 0.08 and an inner wall of at least 30 deg; ejectaAlbedoRatio is the rim-to-2R ring over the 2.5R-4R ring in albedo.jpg (LROC NAC, shading removed; > 1 is brighter ejecta).
boulderTrackCandidates: placements, not detections (3 m boulders and their tracks are below the data's resolution). local is the foot where the ground levels off, wallTop the top of the run.
lowLightPatches: average illumination < 15%, outside permanent shadow, slope < 15 deg (heights smoothed over ~20 m), within 1 km. innerPoint is the point farthest inside the patch.

horizonFromLanding.note: Index = azimuth in degrees (see frame.azimuthConvention). Includes curvature; compare with the Sun/Earth elevation to know if they are above the local horizon.
